newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Avonmore says confident of future.
newsitem.headline: Avonmore says confident of future.

text.p: Irish food group Avonmore Foods Plc said on Monday that it is confident of contintued growth and is focusing on progressing its businesses in the UK and U.S.

"Avonmore is now particularly well resourced to pursue further strategic development," group general manager Pat O'Neill said. "The group is confident of continuing profit and earnings growth in the current year.
Avonmore reported an increase of 13.7 percent in pre-tax profit to 36.45 million Irish pounds for the year to January 4, 1997.
O'Neill the group's operations in Ireland, the UK and U.S. were well established in their respective markets and were adapting well to rapidly changing circumstances.
"Efficiencies continue to be pursued from a competitive cost base," O'Neill said in a results statement.

Strong performances in dairy and agri-trading offset difficulties in some meat sectors and trading was complicated by the unstable currency situation in a number of EU states, O'Neill said. But growing market positions in the United States and Britain provided confidence for the future, he said. The $100 million in new capital raised in the year strengthened the groups's financial position and broadened strategic options, he said.
The group reported adjusted earnings per share up 13.0 percent at 17.19 pence. Turnover grew 7.7 percent to 1,319.43 million Irish pounds while operating profits increased to 46.10 million.
The net interest charge for the year fell to 9.64 million pounds reflecting the level of cash generated, working capital control and management of interest rate exposure, the group said.
The charge also benefitted from the $100 million non-equity capital raised in November through the placement of Preferred Securities with U.S. instititions.
Net borrowings at year-end were 10.10 million Irish pounds against 70.28 million with gearing reduced to 4.0 percent of capital, it said.

The group said a final dividend of 2.60 pence net was being proposed for a total dvidend for the year of 4.50 pence, an increase of 9.8 percent on the 1995 dividend of 4.10 pence. The dividened was covered 3.8 times, it said.
